verdict.rationale: Fivetran does have code-first pieces of its own: the Connector SDK lets you write custom connectors in Python and deploy them, and transformations can run as dbt models imported into your own dbt project. But its core offering is managed, pre-built connectors set up in the dashboard ('no data pipelines to maintain'). The REST API is only a building block for managing that config programmatically. Nothing shows standard pipeline config living as declarative files in your repo, or that it can be moved off Fivetran. missing for 10: declarative pipeline/connection config-as-code (e.g. an official IaC/config-file workflow) for standard connectors, documented versioning and review workflow, portability of pipelines outside Fivetran, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, my pipelines are plain code and config in my own repository — versioned, reviewed, and portable like any software

citations.quote: Fivetran’s Connector SDK allows you to develop a custom data connector using Python and deploy it as an extension of Fivetran.
You can either add the models in the Fivetran dashboard (Quickstart data models) or import them into your dbt project (Fivetran data models).
Use the Fivetran-hosted dbt Core integration or our third-party dbt Cloud and Coalesce orchestration to centralize and manage all your transformations.
